original_question: If G is a connected block graph in which every block has order at least 3, must the nullity of G be at most 1? Here nullity means the number of zero eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G).
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1: whether every connected K2-free block graph has adjacency nullity at most 1.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical content very well: it asks about block graphs, imposes the intended 'no edge-blocks' condition by requiring every block to have order at least 3, and asks for the same spectral conclusion, namely that the adjacency nullity is at most 1. It also correctly identifies nullity as the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 0 of A(G).
missing_details: The paper’s graph class should be named explicitly: a block graph is a simple undirected graph whose blocks (maximal connected subgraphs without a cut-vertex, equivalently maximal 2-connected components together with bridges in the standard convention) are complete graphs.
The paper uses the equivalent shorthand K2-free block graph, meaning that no block is a single edge; equivalently, every block has order at least 3.
The universal quantifier should be made explicit: the question is asking whether the asserted bound holds for every such graph G.
It is helpful to state the standard notation eta(G)=mult_0(A(G)) for the nullity.

To stay paper-faithful, one should not strengthen the hypothesis to the narrower B1^3 condition appearing in the nearby theorem; that stronger condition additionally requires each block to contain at least one non-cut-vertex and leads to nonsingularity, not merely nullity at most 1.
The adjacency matrix should be understood as the ordinary (0,1)-adjacency matrix over the reals for a simple graph.
refined_question: Is it true that for every connected simple block graph G with no block isomorphic to K2 — equivalently, every block of G has order at least 3 — the adjacency nullity eta(G)=mult_0(A(G)) of its (0,1)-adjacency matrix A(G) is at most 1?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s nullity conjecture, not at one of the proved nonsingularity theorems. The exact conjectural content is the 'nullity at most 1' claim for K2-free block graphs; your wording 'every block has order at least 3' is the right graph-theoretic unpacking of K2-free. The nearby context in the corrected follow-up paper defines the narrower class B1^3 and proves that every such graph is nonsingular, which is stronger but applies to a smaller class, so it should not replace the conjecture your draft is trying to capture. One caveat is that the original arXiv submission is withdrawn and its full text was not directly retrievable here; the exact conjectural wording is confirmed by the later note that explicitly says it restates the conjecture from Singh et al. and identifies it there as Conjecture 2.6.
